_comment: Original, paraphrased Clash Royale strategy notes for the RAG advisor (NOT copyrighted text). archetype values match graph/curated.py ARCHETYPE_THREATS keys (or 'general') for retrieval boosting. Numbers are written as words to keep the grounding guardrail clean.

chunks.title: Pull ground win conditions to the centre
chunks.text: A defensive building placed a few tiles in front of the river and nudged toward the centre pulls ground win conditions like Hog Rider and Royal Giant into the middle, where both Princess Towers can shoot them. Placing the building too close to your tower wastes its pull range.

chunks.title: Kite single-target troops to the other lane
chunks.text: A cheap tank such as Ice Golem or Knight dropped in the centre drags single-target ground troops like Mini P.E.K.K.A or Prince across to the opposite lane, buying time and separating the threat from its support.

chunks.title: Split-place at the back to stay reactive
chunks.text: Placing a unit at the back centre lets you react to whichever lane the opponent commits to. Against an unknown deck, play your value defensively first and only counter-push with what survives.

chunks.title: Surround squishy troops with swarms
chunks.text: Drop swarms like Skeletons directly on top of or behind a single-target troop so they wrap around and surround it, landing the most hits before it can retaliate. Never place a swarm in front of the target.

chunks.title: Do not two-spell a cheap threat
chunks.text: Spending two cards to remove one cheap card usually loses the exchange. Hold your small spell for the play it earns the most value against, such as a swarm stacked under your tower.

chunks.title: Out-cycle with a cheap deck
chunks.text: A low average-elixir deck returns to its win condition faster than the opponent can answer it. Defend efficiently, then send the win condition the moment you are up on elixir or have cycled back to it first.

chunks.title: Adjust to double and triple elixir
chunks.text: In double elixir, defences refill quickly so you can afford larger counter-pushes; in single elixir, play patiently and avoid being caught with an empty hand against a big push.

chunks.title: Punish slow big plays in the other lane
chunks.text: When the opponent drops a heavy tank behind their King Tower, immediately apply pressure in the opposite lane to force them to split elixir between attacking and defending.

chunks.title: Defending Lavaloon: protect your anti-air
chunks.text: Against Lava Hound and Balloon your air-targeting units are the whole defence. Keep them spread and out of spell value so a single Lightning or Fireball cannot wipe your air coverage in one shot.

chunks.title: Pull the Lava Hound, save damage for the Balloon
chunks.text: Place your defensive building toward the centre so the Lava Hound drifts inward and both towers help bring it down. Hold your highest single-target damage for the Balloon, which is the real win condition once the Hound pops.

chunks.title: Bait out the Balloon's support spell
chunks.text: Lavaloon relies on Lightning or Zap to clear your swarms before the Balloon connects. Layer your air defence and commit the second wave only after the support spell has been spent.

chunks.title: Use the Lava Hound's slow clock
chunks.text: The Lava Hound is slow, so you usually have time to set up. Do not panic and place everything at once; stagger your defence so the Balloon is met by fresh troops as it crosses the arena.

chunks.title: Defending Golem: kill the support first
chunks.text: Let the Golem walk and put your highest single-target damage on it while clearing the support behind. The Golem does no tower damage until it dies, so removing the support is the priority.

chunks.title: Activate your King Tower with Tornado
chunks.text: Tornado the support troops into your King Tower to switch it on. The extra tower firing dramatically speeds up how quickly you break down a beatdown push.

chunks.title: Turn the Golem defence into a counter-push
chunks.text: Whatever survives your defence becomes offence. Beatdown decks are slow to cycle back, so a single surviving troop alongside your win condition can punish the empty lane hard.

chunks.title: Defending Hog Rider with a building
chunks.text: Hog Rider targets buildings, so a defensive building placed centrally pulls it away from your tower. Add a cheap troop to finish the Hog before it lands a second swing.

chunks.title: Time the building against the Hog
chunks.text: Drop your building as the Hog crosses the river rather than early, so it cannot be pre-baited and the Hog locks onto the building with minimal tower damage.

chunks.title: Defending X-Bow: tank it or rush the other lane
chunks.text: Tank the X-Bow's shots with a high-hitpoint unit while you take it down, or rush the opposite lane so the siege player has to defend instead of charging their X-Bow.

chunks.title: Do not overcommit into siege
chunks.text: X-Bow and Mortar punish overcommitment. Defend with the least elixir possible, then counter-push into the lane they are not defending.

chunks.title: Defending Graveyard with reactive splash
chunks.text: Place a splash unit on the centre of the targeted tower tile so it hits skeletons as they spawn around it. Reacting beats pre-placing, because the skeletons spawn where your tower is being attacked.

chunks.title: Expect a spell with the Graveyard
chunks.text: A Graveyard usually comes with Poison or Tornado. Keep your splasher out of the Poison radius and do not rely on a single swarm to clear the skeletons.

chunks.title: Defending P.E.K.K.A bridge spam
chunks.text: Bridge spam wins by catching you off guard at the bridge. Keep defensive elixir in hand, answer the P.E.K.K.A with a building or swarm, and kite the Bandit and Battle Ram apart.

chunks.title: Kite the slow P.E.K.K.A
chunks.text: The P.E.K.K.A is slow and single-target. Pull it to the centre with a cheap troop so it never reaches a tower, then swarm it from behind while it is occupied.

chunks.title: Defending Mega Knight: never clump
chunks.text: The Mega Knight's jump and spawn damage punish grouped troops. Meet it with a single tank-killer and hold your swarm until after it has landed.

chunks.title: Spend bait spells on value
chunks.text: Bait decks want you to waste your small spell early. Use Log or Arrows on the highest-value target, such as the Goblin Barrel on your tower or the Princess, not the first cheap troop you see.

chunks.title: Defending Royal Giant
chunks.text: Place a building to drag the Royal Giant off your tower and stack a high-damage unit behind it. Punish the opposite lane, since Royal Giant decks are often passive.

chunks.title: Defending Sparky: reset or distract
chunks.text: Reset Sparky's charge with a Zap or Electro Wizard, or distract it with a cheap swarm so it wastes its shot. Never let it fire into a clustered defence.

chunks.title: Spread anti-air against spells
chunks.text: When your only reliable anti-air is one or two units, keep them apart so a single splash spell cannot remove your whole air defence. Deploy them deep and let the air push come to them.
